sections.h2: Where do Buchanan County property taxes get billed and collected?
sections.html:
Both the Assessor and the Collector work from the Buchanan County courthouse complex at 411 Jules Street in St. Joseph. The Collector is in Room 123 (816-271-1401, fax 816-271-1584), and the Assessor is in Rooms 122 and 222 (816-271-1520). Both offices keep Monday to Friday hours, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM.

The Collector's page says the office handles about $100 million in tax revenue each year and passes it to 33 taxing districts. It also prepares the statements, issues Merchant and Manufacturer licenses and runs the delinquent tax sale each August. The Assessor, an elected official, maintains a roll of more than 40,000 real parcels and over 110,000 articles of personal property.

sections.h2: What is Buchanan County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Buchanan County covers 415 square miles along the Missouri River in the northwest corner of the state. Its seat, St. Joseph, held 72,473 people in 2020, far more than Gower, Agency, Dearborn or any other community. The county was organized in 1838 as Roberts County and renamed in 1839 for James Buchanan. Interstate 29, Interstate 229 and U.S. 36, 59, 71 and 169 are the main roads.

Several school systems serve the county: St. Joseph School District, Buchanan County R-IV at De Kalb, East Buchanan County C-1 at Gower, Mid-Buchanan County R-V at Faucett, and the North Platte County R-I district. Missouri Western State University is in St. Joseph. The population has slipped, from 89,201 in 2010 to an estimated 83,540 in 2025.

sections.h2: How do Buchanan County housing numbers compare?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists the following for Buchanan County.

  • Housing units in 2025: 38,615
  • Owner-occupied rate, 2020-2024: 66.3 percent
  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $166,300
  • Median gross rent: $902
  • Median household income: $62,158
  • Building permits in 2025: 52

With the 19 percent residential rate that Boone County's Collector publishes for Missouri, a $166,300 home comes to roughly $31,597 of assessed value. Taxing districts then apply their levies per $100 of that figure. The Assessor's page explains that the Assessor finishes the roll by about July 1 and sends it to the County Clerk, that districts set budgets and levies near the end of September, and that the Assessor has no part in setting those levies.

sections.h2: When does Buchanan County want its tax payments?
sections.html:
Statements go out during the first week of November. The Collector asks for payment upon receipt, and December 31 is the line between on time and late. A payment counts only if it arrives by then or carries an official United States Postal Service postmark, since a private postage meter mark is not accepted. State law on mailed payments appears in RSMo 139.100.

If no statement shows up by the end of November, contact the office for a copy. Not getting one does not waive interest or penalties. Anyone who needs a receipt within seven days should pay in person, since a receipt for an online payment is mailed in three to five business days. The office takes cash, check, American Express, Discover, MasterCard and Visa, but not payments by phone, and a lost receipt can be replaced for $1.

sections.h2: What are the Buchanan County property tax steps in order?
sections.html:
The table collects dates from the Collector's and Assessor's pages and from the state's tax appeal guidance.

sections.h2: What happens if Buchanan County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquent real estate and personal property taxes are applied first. The Collector's page says any back taxes owed must be paid before a payment goes toward the current year, and that a payment schedule printed on the statement applies after December 31.

Land that reaches the back tax book picks up a penalty of 18 percent of the year's delinquency under RSMo 140.100, limited to 2 percent per month if the owner redeems before the sale. RSMo 140.150 allows sale of delinquent land on the fourth Monday in August, requires the Collector to mail a first class notice to the recorded owner, and adds a certified mailing when the assessed value tops $1,000. The owner can pay the tax, penalty and costs at any point before the sale.

sections.h2: What property tax relief exists for Buchanan County seniors?
sections.html:
Two programs show up on the county's website. The Missouri Property Tax Credit can return up to $750 to residents who are 65 or older, 100 percent disabled, or a veteran disabled by service, or who are 60 or older and receive surviving spouse Social Security benefits. Household income, Social Security included, cannot exceed $25,000 for a single filer or $27,000 for a married couple. The Department of Revenue's number is 573-751-3505, and Form MO-PTC is available by calling 800-877-6881.

The Buchanan County Commission also voted in September 2024 to offer the Senior Citizen Homestead Property Tax Credit under RSMo 137.1050. Residents aged 62 or older can freeze the amount owed on a primary residence at its level for the year they qualify, which is the 2024 amount for those eligible then. It limits future increases only and gives no refund. The first application window ran March 1 through June 30, 2025, so ask the courthouse about any later window.

sections.h2: What should a St. Joseph seller know about tax and recording timing?
sections.html:
A sale does not erase the year's bill, so settle who pays what before closing day. Ask the Collector's office for the current balance on the parcel, and remember that back taxes must be cleared before any money counts toward the current year. Questions about a name, mailing address or legal description belong to the Assessor, not the Collector.

The Recorder of Deeds is in Room 103 of the same building at 411 Jules Street, phone 816-271-1437. That office will not record anything after 4:00 PM. Papers handed in later are recorded in the order received starting at 8:00 AM the next business day, which matters when a closing runs late near December 31 or a payoff deadline. The Recorder also says it cannot prepare a deed or answer legal questions, so use a title company or attorney for the paperwork.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Buchanan County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the Assessor's office, which can explain how a value was reached. If the answer is unsatisfactory, the Board of Equalization is the next stop, with a filing deadline of the second Monday in July. The State Tax Commission's guidance says a later appeal to the Commission follows the board's decision by 30 days, and RSMo 138.430 sets that right.

An owner who has paid without protest and skipped both appeals cannot challenge that year's assessment, but may appeal the next year. Property held by an LLC, trust, estate or corporation must use an attorney for a State Tax Commission appeal.

faqs.q: What is the due date for Buchanan County property tax?
faqs.a: December 31. Payment must reach the Collector or carry an official USPS postmark by that day, since private postage meter marks do not count.

faqs.q: Where is the Buchanan County Collector located?
faqs.a: At 411 Jules Street, Room 123, in St. Joseph. Hours are 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM Monday through Friday, and the number is 816-271-1401.

faqs.q: Can I pay Buchanan County taxes online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the county's Pay/View Taxes application, which adds a convenience fee that the Collector neither sets nor keeps. Pay in person if you need a receipt in under seven days.

faqs.q: When is the Buchanan County tax sale?
faqs.a: The Collector holds it each August. State law places delinquent land sales on the fourth Monday in August, and the 2026 sale date has passed.

faqs.q: Is there a senior tax freeze in Buchanan County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county adopted the Senior Citizen Homestead Property Tax Credit in September 2024 for residents 62 and older. It caps future increases on a primary residence and is not a refund.
